Run pool items only with thyrox -p

The executor's directive: thyrox is the only client. Talking to
Anthropic or any other provider is thyrox's job, through its
translators and credential selection, not a second client's.

headless-pool no longer lets HEADLESS_POOL_CLAUDE point the items at
claude -p: declaring it refuses with exit 2 and names
HEADLESS_POOL_RUNNER, which only declares a test double that speaks the
thyrox -p contract. Items receive the cache TTL as
THYROX_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL alone; the CLAUDE_CODE_ copy had no reader
left. The list of host credentials the pool strips from an item's
environment is unchanged.

print.ts, pool_history, the rule and .env.example now call thyrox -p
the contract and cite the executable's --print mode as its source. The
Bedrock switch keeps CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK because the provider still
reads that name; both move together in the identifier phase.
